column1: # A pair here is reachable only through the reference's sloppy path:
# EwtsConverter.toUnicode(str) calls toUnicode(str, null, true, false), and
# sloppy = true runs normalizeSloppyWylie first. Our strict W->U does not read
# it, so in step 4.4 (Q-5, 17.10.2026) the pair moved out of java_ewts.tsv into
# this file, and the strict W->U count fell from 6 to 5.
# Nothing reads this file yet. It is checked in wave 6, together with the sloppy
# mode and the aliases normalizeSloppyWylie applies (Ny -> ny, Ng -> ng,
# Ts -> ts, Dz -> dz, G/K/C/B/P/L/Z/J lowered, adm -> ad+m, " m " -> " ma ",
# H and M lowered after a vowel, S -> s but not Sh). The reference methods
# textConvertSloppy() and normalizeSloppyWylie() hold the rest of that material;
# it gets its own rows when the mode exists.
# Columns: wylie <TAB> unicode  (the sloppy conversion of the wylie).
